headline: High: EMQX’s broad network egress paired with Great Expectations’ file-based validation can create default data-leak and compliance risks; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are lower but present via shared artifacts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: EMQX exposes HTTP API output and Great Expectations consumes files, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry attacker-controlled content into validation artifacts. The profiles do not show a shared channel by default, so this is not medium. Both agents are open-source and unverified, so uncertainty keeps it above none.
conditions: IF EMQX output is copied into a Great Expectations input file without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF a shared workspace is used for both agents, file content can be treated as instructions by downstream tooling.
mitigations: Use a read-only handoff file for EMQX outputs.
Strip executable markup from any copied content.
Separate the agents into different directories.
Add a human review step before Great Expectations consumes EMQX-generated artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and touches IoT data, while Great Expectations reads and writes validation files and documentation. If the same workspace or dataset is shared, sensitive IoT data can flow into validation outputs or logs. The profiles do not show secrets handling, but the file-and-egress combination makes leakage plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF EMQX outputs IoT payloads into files that Great Expectations reads, those payloads can be copied into validation results.
IF Great Expectations artifacts are stored in a shared workspace, downstream access can expose the same data class.
mitigations: Store EMQX outputs in a separate directory.
Exclude sensitive fields before validation.
Disable or minimize logging of sample rows.
Review Great Expectations result artifacts before sharing them.
Use synthetic data for validation runs where possible.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and Great Expectations can install packages, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource or shared locks. That makes direct capability conflict possible only under unusual orchestration, not by default. Uncertainty does not justify medium because no shared writable surface is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF package installation by Great Expectations modifies a shared environment, dependency drift can affect EMQX workflows.
mitigations: Pin package versions for Great Expectations.
Run each agent in its own environment.
Avoid sharing a writable working directory.
Use separate virtual environments or containers.

D_cascading_error.rationale: EMQX can emit network-facing outputs and Great Expectations can consume files as validation inputs, so A’s output may become B’s input without a documented verification step. Great Expectations is not shown to critically evaluate EMQX provenance, so erroneous or manipulated data could cascade into misleading validation results. The pair is not documented enough for high.
conditions: IF EMQX-generated data is fed directly into Great Expectations expectations, errors can propagate.
IF validation results are treated as authoritative without manual review, downstream decisions can be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a schema check before validation.
Require a human review of EMQX-derived inputs.
Compare results against a known-good baseline.
Mark EMQX-derived datasets as untrusted in documentation.

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while Great Expectations stores validation results and documentation. If IoT data includes regulated personal data, moving it into Great Expectations artifacts can create retention and residency mismatches. Only one agent needs citation here because the compliance issue is the data flow into B’s files; the pairwise risk is inferred from A’s data class and B’s storage surfaces.
conditions: IF IoT data contains personal data subject to retention limits, Great Expectations artifacts may violate policy.
IF validation outputs are stored longer than source data, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify IoT fields before validation.
Set a short retention period for validation artifacts.
Redact personal data from reports.
Document the data flow and retention owner.
